L3.1.quote: proved (and verified by brute force) that optimal play = greedy, so LB gets odd-position pieces (sorted decreasing). Game reduces to: LB picks ≤ n+1 pieces (composition of 1), XY subdivides with ≤ n cuts, payoff = alternating sum $D = p_1 - p_2 + p_3 - \cdots$; LB share $= (1+D)/2$.
L3.1.note: Correct reduction is stated, but optimal greedy play is only asserted, not argued.

L3.2.quote: Part B (XY always forces $D\le T_n$) still open: best candidate "min over subsets of greedy chain $\le T_n S$" — needs verification & proof.
L3.2.note: The pigeonhole attempt has a recognized realizability gap; no universal Xiang construction is proved.

L3.3.quote: family $a_1\le\cdots\le a_m$ super-increasing with margin $\delta$ ($a_1\ge\delta$, $a_{i+1}\ge\delta+a_1+\cdots+a_i$), subdivided with $\le m-1$ cuts ⇒ $D\ge\delta$. Proof: take optimal matching $\mu$; build multigraph on pieces (edge = matched pair of fragments, unmatched frag = mark).
L3.3.note: The matching, tree-component, slack, signed-sum, and block-lemma argument covers arbitrary replies and all n.

parsed.notes: The lower bound is substantively argued for the geometric division. The upper bound remains explicitly open, and the claiming-phase reduction lacks its promised proof.
